newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen up 83-93 bcf in weekly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen up 83-93 bcf in weekly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to rise by 83 to 93 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for an overall build ranged from 80.5 bcf to 100 bcf for the week ended September 6. The four-week average is 84.5 bcf.

"A lot of gas was put into storage over the Labor Day weekend, but historically the number should be lower than last week," said one trader, noting the traditional start to the withdrawal season was only about seven weeks away.
Other traders thought this year's number would defy historical data as the Producing Region still lagged far behind year-ago inventories.

Year-ago levels posted a 20 bcf gain to 78 percent of capacity. In AGA's last report, stocks rose by 30 bcf in the Producing Region to only 54 percent of capacity, which was 13 percent behind the total U.S. tally.
Last week, AGA showed overall stocks rose by 94 bcf to 67 percent, which was above most expectations, but were still 423 bcf below the same year-ago period.
Last year at this time, stocks rose by 76 bcf.
